groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

Many schools in Singapore are currently grappling with a severe lack of canteen vendors. Individual stallholders often find it difficult to operate with many financial __(16: constraints)__. Moreover, the rising cost of ingredients and a lack of manpower have forced many vendors to __(17: cease)__ operations. To address this issue, several schools are exploring alternatives such as the central kitchen model.
Under the new model, catering companies will supply meals directly to the schools. Students will be able to collect their pre-ordered food __(18: seamlessly)__ from automated machines using their smart cards. Vendors will also be able to cater to the __(19: dietary)__ needs of students more effectively. Schools believe this innovative approach will ensure that students can obtain their meals __(20: promptly)__. This will reduce the time needed to wait in queues during their recess break.

Study the texts and then answer questions 21 to 25.

++Text 1++
The text below shows a poster for a school bag.
[[img1]]
++Text 2++
The extract below is taken from an online article.
School bags are designed to be both functional and trendy, which makes them appealing to students. Lately, more focus has been put on making school bags look good. For many students, their school bag is also a way to express their personality and personal style. Is that true for you, too?
While it may seem exciting to fit everything into one stylish bag, have you considered the impact on your health? Carrying too many items or a heavy bag strains your back. This may cause short-term discomfort and lead to long-term posture problems. To cushion the effect, you should carry a school bag that fits comfortably on your back. Features such as wide straps and padded backs help distribute weight more evenly. By choosing a school bag wisely, you can reduce the pressure on your back.
Ultimately, health experts recommend packing only the items needed for the day to keep your school bag light. For example, store certain items in your school locker or keep some materials under your desk if your school allows it. By planning what you bring each day and leaving out unnecessary items, you can protect your back and still have everything you need.

images.alt: Poster. Heading: Peaks School Bag. Carry Everything in Style. Say goodbye to boring school bags! Fit your entire school day into one bag, all your books, stationery, lunch boxes and more! Get organised with a specific space for everything! No more mess or things left behind! In the middle is a picture of a backpack with a front zip pocket. On its left: Suitable for students of all ages! On its right: Wide range of colours to choose from! Below: Designed with you in mind! At the bottom, beside a photo of a boy carrying a school bag: "I love my Peaks school bag! Everything I need for school fits comfortably into it. I can also find and take out any item I need easily!" - Ansel, 12-year-old student

groups.text:
There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
**EACH WORD CAN BE USED ONLY ++ONCE++.**
[[table1]]

Plastic waste is everywhere. Every day, an astonishing amount of plastic waste enough to fill 2,000 garbage trucks __(26)__ dumped into the ocean. Plastic litter can be found at the bottom of the ocean and on top of Mount Everest. Surprisingly, plastic waste has now turned __(27)__ on the backs of hermit crabs!
Hermit crabs are tiny animals with soft, curly bodies __(28)__ leave them vulnerable to predators. __(29)__ their tails are fragile, they must constantly look for empty shells to protect __(30)__ from hungry birds and fishes. Studies show 10 out of 16 land species __(31)__ been observed wearing plastic waste, such as bottle caps, and __(32)__ broken lightbulbs.
Scientists believe this unusual behaviour may be due to the declining population of sea snails, resulting __(33)__ fewer natural shells for the crabs. It is also possible that crabs choose plastic materials __(34)__ traditional shells because they are lighter in weight and easier to carry.
While scientists agree that plastic pollution harms wildlife and ecosystems, it is still unclear __(35)__ hermit crabs are directly endangered by this behaviour. This shows that plastic waste can affect even small animals.
Adapted from https://www.timeforkids.com/g56/creative-crabs

Each of the underlined words contains either a spelling or grammatical error. Write the correct word in each of the boxes.

Last week, I went to a local theatre to see a performance of Chicken Little. The story followed a clear __(36: sequanse)__ of events that everyone could easily follow. It began when a small object __(37: accidental)__ hit the main character, making her think the sky was falling. Overwhelmed by fear, she quickly __(38: spreading)__ her panic all the other animals in the woods.
I __(39: thurruhly)__ enjoyed the acting of the performers. Their high-energy __(40: seens)__ made the play realistic and comical. They cleverly used fast __(41: dielog)__ to show how confused they were as they ran around the stage. In the final act, the characters realised the importance of not __(42: jump)__ to conclusions.
It provided plenty of laughter while conveying a __(43: valued)__ lesson about seeking the truth. I would certainly __(44: rekkomend)__ this show to anyone who __(45: enjoying)__ a fun story with a deep meaning. The performance is a perfect example of how theatre can teach us important things while making us laugh.

Fill in each blank with a suitable word.

Blind boxes are small toys sold in sealed packaging. Buyers do not know what they will get __(46)__ they open them. Although blind boxes feel like a modern trend, the idea is not __(47)__. In the 1950's, mystery prize tickets, also __(48)__ as Tikam-Tikam, were so common in Singapore that every street corner had a vendor selling them. The 1950's Tikam-Tikam craze led many children and even adults to extreme __(49)__ such as shoplifting just to get what they want. In __(50)__ months, such acts have also been reported by shops selling blind boxes here.
So __(51)__ are blind boxes so appealing? One reason is our human desire to collect. People enjoy gathering complete sets, especially when some items are __(52)__ in quantity. When a rare piece is finally found, it feels as if a difficult __(53)__ has been successfully completed. Another reason is social influence where collectors share their __(54)__ online through posts and live videos. Seeing others unbox rare items creates excitement and encourages more people to __(55)__ the trend.
However, the randomness of blind boxes creates a cycle of anticipation __(56)__ to gambling. People keep buying more boxes in __(57)__ of getting a rare item, only to end up with duplicates. Over time, this cycle can be hard to __(58)__ and the behaviour may even become addictive. This leads to risky spending __(59)__ where people frequently spend more than intended or buy repeatedly without realising how quickly the cost is adding up. As a result, governments are considering rules and __(60)__ to better protect consumers, like the ban on Tikam-Tikam in 1961. Although blind boxes can be fun, it is important to know the potential harms and act responsibly.
Adapted from https://medium.com/publiclibrarysg/the-blind-box-boom-why-everyone-is-going-crazy-for-mystery-collectibles

Read the passage below and answer questions 66 to 75.

**1** The first night of the Primary 5 camp was difficult for Ryan. As the dormitory lights dimmed, the quiet forest outside made **his heart beat faster**. Unlike Marcus, who was already snoring loudly, Ryan lay sleepless in the dark. This was his first time staying away from home, and the thin, hard mattress made him miss his own comfortable bed.
**2** The next morning, the students headed to the High Elements course, which began with a daunting ten-metre climb. Marcus was appointed the group leader, and it was no surprise — during the practice sessions in school, he was the only one who had mastered all the safety knots. After putting on his safety gear, he checked every classmate's harness with a sharp gaze. Mr Lim, their form teacher, stood at the side observing him quietly, his clipboard tucked under his arm.
**3** Marcus scaled the rock wall with ease, but when it was Ryan's turn, his legs began to shake like jelly. He took one look at the sheer height of the wall and froze. "Ryan! Don't just stand there! Start climbing! Everyone else is waiting for you," Marcus shouted from above. Ryan felt **embarrassed**. His face turned a deep crimson as the other students watched him tremble.
**4** Later that afternoon, the class went for a long hiking expedition. Exhausted, Ryan had slowed and was lagging behind. He often stopped to catch his breath. Marcus had a single-minded will to be the first group to reach the checkpoint. Suddenly, he snatched Ryan's water bottle. "You're drinking too much and stopping too often!" Marcus shouted. He shoved the bottle into his own bag and stomped off. Ryan stared wide-eyed at Marcus's back. The outburst caused the class to stop and murmur. Ryan felt his eyes moisten, but he forced himself to keep walking in silence. From the back of the group, Mr Lim saw everything but kept his distance.
**5** By evening, Ryan was in a sullen mood. During dinner, he sat alone at the edge of the campsite. "All Marcus cares about is that silly trophy," he muttered under his breath.
**6** That night, Ryan could not sleep. He slipped out to the washroom to splash some water on his face. Near the benches, he heard soft sobbing. To his surprise, he saw Marcus sitting on the ground with his head between his knees. Marcus was holding the brass compass so tightly that his knuckles were white. Ryan froze. His first instinct was to walk away, but remembering how Marcus had treated him, he decided to stay and taunt his tormentor. However, as he watched Marcus shaking, his anger began to soften. Then he noticed an inscription on the back of the compass: Best Camper. Realising that the compass held sentimental value for Marcus, Ryan felt a lump forming in his throat.
**7** "It's just a camp, Marcus," Ryan said gently. Marcus jumped and tried to hide **++it++**. "Go away," he snapped, but his voice was shaky and lacked its usual confidence. Ryan sat down nearby. "I'm so homesick I can't even eat," he admitted. Marcus finally relaxed and held up the compass. "This was my brother's. He had won 'Best Camper' three years ago. My parents expect me to be just like him, but it's a **Herculean task**." Ryan finally understood why Marcus had behaved the way he did — he was terrified of letting his family down.
**8** The next morning, during the outdoor cooking session, Ryan struggled to light his fire. The tiny flame kept flickering out in the breeze, and his pot of water remained cold. Before he could give up, Marcus came over and crouched beside him. "Stack the fuel tablets like this. It keeps the flame going," he said, arranging them. He used his own body to block the wind while Ryan tried again. When the fire was lit, Ryan watched the steady glow with a grateful smile.
**9** From across the campsite, Mr Lim watched the interaction between the two boys. **He nodded approvingly, thinking that sometimes, the most important lessons at camp had nothing to do with knots or rock walls.**

questions.stem:
The pictures below show Elsie visiting to a fire station. Study the pictures carefully.
[[img1]]
++Your Task++
Imagine you are Elsie.
**Write an article for the class noticeboard to tell your classmates about your experience visiting a fire station.**
You are to refer to the pictures and information above for your article. The bullet point underlined below requires you to come up with your own information.

In your writing, include the following key information:
- why you visited a fire station
- how you prepared for the visit
- two things you were allowed to do during the visit
- one other detail about the visit
- ++one way you have benefitted from the visit++

You may reorder the points. Remember to write in complete sentences.

images.alt: Four numbered pictures. Picture 1: Elsie's mother holds a phone and says, 'Elsie, City Fire Station is having an open house. Would you like to attend it?' Elsie raises her fist happily and replies, 'That sounds interesting! I'll check the open house programme and plan how we'll spend our time there.' Picture 2: A firefighter hands Elsie a helmet and says, 'You can try wearing a firefighter's helmet, mask and uniform!' Her mother stands beside her. Picture 3: Elsie, now wearing a firefighter's helmet and uniform, stands by a fire engine with its door open. A firefighter asks, 'Would you like to get into the fire engine?' and she answers, 'Yes, please!' Picture 4: Elsie and her mother walk away from a building with the sign CITY FIRE STATION. Elsie says, 'I enjoyed watching the firefighters demonstrate how they respond to various emergencies, Mum. They are so brave!'

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your writing against the points below.

explanation: Purpose: to tell your classmates about your experience visiting a fire station. Audience: your classmates. Context: an article for the class noticeboard, written as Elsie. Write 'I', not 'Elsie'.
Format: an article needs a title (for example 'My Visit to City Fire Station') and your name as the writer. It is not a letter or an email, so no 'Dear classmates' and no sign-off.
Point 1, why you visited: City Fire Station was having an open house and your mother asked if you would like to attend it.
Point 2, how you prepared: you checked the open house programme and planned how you and your mother would spend your time there.
Point 3, two things you were allowed to do: try wearing a firefighter's helmet, mask and uniform; get into the fire engine. Give both.

Point 4, one other detail: you watched the firefighters demonstrate how they respond to various emergencies (or: the visit was at City Fire Station; you went with your mother; you found the firefighters very brave).
Point 5, one way you have benefitted (your own idea, it is not in the pictures): for example, you now know what to do in an emergency, or you appreciate how hard firefighters work to keep us safe.

Tone: friendly and enthusiastic, suitable for classmates, but in complete, correct sentences. Use the past tense for what happened. 6 marks are for covering all the points for the task; 8 marks are for language and organisation.

review.solvedAnswer: Checklist written from the task and pictures.
review.note: The paper prints 'visiting to a fire station' in the first line; it is transcribed as printed. The speech bubbles have pencil underlining from a previous owner, which gives nothing away.

questions.stem:
Write a composition of ++at least 150 words++ about **showing respect**.
The pictures are provided to help you think about this topic.
Your composition should be based on one or more of these pictures.
[[img1]]
Consider the following points when you plan your composition:
- Why was there a need to show respect?
- How was respect shown?

You may use the points in any order and include other relevant points as well.

images.alt: Three pictures in a column. Picture 1: a wristwatch showing the time. Picture 2: a loudspeaker blasting loud music, with musical notes and lightning-shaped sound lines around it. Picture 3: a dining table laid for a meal with plates of food, cutlery, glasses and a bottle, and chairs around it.

answer.value: There is no single model answer. Check your plan and your story against the points below.

explanation: The topic is 'showing respect'. The whole story must lead to a moment where someone shows respect (or learns to), and you must use at least one picture as an important part of the story, not just mention it.

Picture 1, the watch: respecting other people's time. For example, a character who is always late keeps a team, a coach or a grandparent waiting, sees the trouble it causes, and learns to be punctual.

Picture 2, the loudspeaker: respecting other people's need for peace and quiet. For example, blasting music while a neighbour's baby sleeps or a sibling studies for an exam, then turning it down and apologising.

Picture 3, the dining table: respecting elders, hosts or other cultures at a meal. For example, waiting for the elders to start eating, putting the phone away, or trying a dish that a host has taken hours to prepare.
Answer both guiding points clearly: why respect was needed (who was affected and how they felt) and how it was shown (a clear action, not just 'I was respectful').
Story arc: a setting and characters, a problem where respect is missing or tested, a turning point where the character realises it, the respectful action, and the result.

Ending: return to the topic. Say what the character learnt about showing respect and how it changed the way he or she behaves. 18 marks are for content and 18 for language and organisation, so check tenses, paragraphing and vocabulary.

review.solvedAnswer: Planning checklist written from the topic and pictures.

questions.stem: "I am really looking forward to __________ the new science centre during our next learning journey," exclaimed Michelle.

explanation: Rule: in 'look forward to', the word 'to' is a preposition, not part of a to-infinitive. A verb that follows a preposition takes the -ing form.
So we say 'looking forward to visiting', just like 'looking forward to seeing you'.
'visit' is the tempting wrong answer because 'to visit' looks right, but 'look forward to visit' is wrong.
The answer is option (4), visiting.

questions.stem: "You spent two hours watching videos? __________ unacceptable!" Dad said sternly.

explanation: Dad is talking about one thing: the fact that the child spent two hours watching videos. One thing needs a singular word, so 'These are' and 'Those are' are out.
Rule: use 'that' to point back to something that has just been said or has already happened. 'This' points to something here and now, or something you are about to say.
The two hours of videos are already over and have just been mentioned, so Dad says 'That is unacceptable!'
The answer is option (2), That is.

questions.stem: The captain of the badminton team, together with his team members, __________ hard every afternoon for the upcoming competition.

explanation: Rule: words added with 'together with', 'as well as' or 'along with' are not part of the subject. The verb agrees with the first noun only.
Cover up 'together with his team members'. The subject is 'The captain', which is singular.
'every afternoon' shows a habit, so use the simple present: singular subject + trains. 'training' cannot stand alone without 'is'.
'train' and 'have trained' are plural forms; they are tempting only if you count the team members. The answer is option (2), trains.

questions.stem: "Since the talk ended late, there is __________ time left for us to go to the playground," Sally told her friends.

explanation: 'time' cannot be counted, so 'few' and 'many' (for countable nouns) are out.
The talk ended late, so there is hardly any time left. 'little' means 'almost none' and is used with uncountable nouns.
'much' would mean a lot of time, which does not fit 'ended late'. Also, we do not normally say 'there is much time' in a positive sentence.
The answer is option (2), little.

questions.stem: "Learning a new language __________ easy so far, but I am enjoying the challenge," said Mr Tan.

explanation: Clue: 'so far' means from some time in the past up to now. That signals the present perfect tense: has/have + past participle.
The subject 'Learning a new language' is one activity, so it is singular: 'has not been'.
'had not been' (past perfect) is for something before another past event, but Mr Tan is still learning ('I am enjoying'). 'is not' and 'was not' do not go with 'so far'.
The answer is option (3), has not been.

questions.stem: You will not be able to join the dance team __________ you pass the audition next Tuesday.

explanation: The sentence gives a condition: passing the audition is the only way to join the team.
'unless' means 'if ... not'. 'You will not be able to join unless you pass' = 'You will not be able to join if you do not pass'.
'since' gives a reason, 'although' shows contrast and 'whereas' compares two things. None of them sets a condition.
The answer is option (2), unless.

questions.stem: "She'll be representing our school in the storytelling competition, __________?" asked the principal.

explanation: Rule: a question tag repeats the helping verb of the statement. A positive statement takes a negative tag.
'She'll' is short for 'She will'. The helping verb is 'will', and its negative is 'won't'.
'wouldn't she' would match 'She'd' (she would), and 'isn't she' would match 'She's'. Read the short form carefully.
The answer is option (2), won't she.

questions.stem: The football match was postponed __________ the thunderstorm warning.

explanation: The thunderstorm warning is the reason the match was postponed, so we need a phrase that means 'because of'.
'in view of' means 'because of' or 'considering'.
'in line with' means following a rule or matching something, 'on behalf of' means representing someone, and 'with reference to' means 'about' (used in letters). None of them gives a reason.
The answer is option (1), in view of.

questions.stem: Madam Tan reprimanded her son, "You __________ left home earlier to avoid being caught in the heavy rain on your way to school."

explanation: 'reprimanded' means scolded. Madam Tan is telling her son what the right thing to do was, which he did not do.
Rule: 'should have' + past participle is used for something that was the right thing to do but was not done.
'could have' only says it was possible, which is too weak for a scolding. 'must have' means you are sure it happened, but he did not leave early.
The answer is option (4), should have.

review.note: The key's digit for Q9 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a 4, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: "I witnessed the boy __________ the road before the traffic light turned green," the security guard reported.

explanation: Rule: after verbs of the senses (see, watch, hear, notice, witness) + a person, use the base form of the verb for a complete action: 'I saw him cross the road.'
'witnessed' already carries the past tense. The second verb does not take a tense, so 'crosses', 'crossed' and 'had crossed' are all wrong.
'crossed' is the tempting one because the event is in the past, but only the first verb shows the tense.
The answer is option (1), cross.

questions.stem: After years of volunteering at the animal shelter, Jane has developed a strong __________ with the staff and the rescued animals.

explanation: 'rapport' means a close, friendly relationship in which people understand each other. We 'develop a rapport **with**' someone.
Years of volunteering would build that kind of bond with both the staff and the animals.

'familiarity' is tempting, but it only means knowing something well, and we do not say 'a strong familiarity'. 'influence' goes with 'on' or 'over', and a 'reputation' is what others think of you, not something you have 'with the animals'.
The answer is option (1), rapport.

questions.stem: Even when faced with an angry and demanding customer, the manager remained __________ and calmly addressed the complaints.

explanation: Clue: 'calmly addressed the complaints'. We need a word that means calm and in control of your feelings.
'composed' means exactly that: calm and not showing anger or nervousness.
'cautious' means careful to avoid danger, 'courageous' means brave, and 'comforting' means making someone feel better. None of them matches 'calmly'.
The answer is option (2), composed.

questions.stem: Before submitting his final writing draft, Josh checked his work __________, scrutinising every word to ensure there were no grammatical mistakes.

explanation: Clue: 'scrutinising every word'. To scrutinise is to examine very closely.
'meticulously' means very carefully, paying attention to every small detail.
'briefly' (for a short time) is the opposite. 'routinely' means as a regular habit and 'confidently' means feeling sure; neither tells us he checked every word.
The answer is option (4), meticulously.

questions.stem: When the fire alarm rang, the security guard immediately __________ the situation to determine if it was a real emergency.

explanation: The guard wanted 'to determine if it was a real emergency', so he investigated.
'look into' means to investigate or find out the facts about a situation or problem.
'look over' means to check something quickly, such as a piece of work. 'look through' means to read or search through papers or a bag. 'look for' means to search for something lost.
The answer is option (2), looked into.

questions.stem: Samuel knew he had to __________ the opportunity and sign up for the leadership camp as the slots were limited.

explanation: Clue: 'the slots were limited', so he had to act quickly before the chance was gone.
'seize the opportunity' is a fixed expression that means to grab a chance eagerly and quickly.
'miss' is the opposite of what he had to do. The opportunity already existed, so he did not need to 'find' or 'create' it.
The answer is option (3), seize.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++constraints++.

explanation: 'constraints' are things that limit what you can do. 'Financial constraints' means not having enough money to do what you want.
'limitations' has the same meaning: financial limitations.
'burdens' is tempting because money problems are heavy to bear, but a burden is a load or duty, not a limit. 'setbacks' are events that delay progress.
The answer is option (3), limitations.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++cease++.

explanation: To 'cease' is to stop completely. The vendors were forced to close their stalls.
'discontinue' means to stop doing something for good.
'pause' is tempting, but a pause is only a short stop before carrying on again. The passage says there is a 'severe lack' of vendors, so they have stopped for good.
The answer is option (4), discontinue.

review.note: The key's digit for Q17 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a 4, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++seamlessly++.

explanation: A seam is a join. 'Seamlessly' means with no breaks, hitches or problems.
Collecting pre-ordered food from a machine with one tap of a smart card happens 'smoothly'.
'systematically' means following a fixed step-by-step method, and 'independently' means on your own. Those are about how the students act, not about how trouble-free the collection is.
The answer is option (2), smoothly.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++dietary++.

explanation: 'dietary' comes from 'diet', the food a person eats. 'Dietary needs' are needs about what a person should or should not eat.
'nutritional' is about food and the nourishment it gives, so it is the closest.
'medical' is tempting because some food needs come from allergies, but dietary needs are about food in general, not about illness and treatment.
The answer is option (4), nutritional.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++promptly++.

explanation: 'promptly' means quickly and without delay.
Clue: the next sentence says this 'will reduce the time needed to wait in queues'. So the point is time, and 'on time' is the closest.
'with ease' means without difficulty, which is closer to 'seamlessly' in question 18, not to 'promptly'.
The answer is option (1), on time.

questions.stem: "Carry Everything in Style." The purpose of this statement in Text 1 is to __________.
options: highlight that the bag is useful and trendy
remind students of what they must carry to school
encourage students to care about how they look

explanation: Break the slogan into two halves. 'Carry Everything' says the bag is useful: it holds all your things. 'in Style' says the bag is trendy and looks good.
Only option (2) covers both halves: useful and trendy.
Option (1) is the tempting one, but storage capacity explains only 'Carry Everything' and leaves out 'in Style'. Option (4) covers only 'Style'.
The answer is option (2).

review.note: In option (3) the words after 'carry' are damaged in the scan and written over by hand; it is read as 'carry to school'.

questions.stem: Why was Ansel featured in Text 1?
options: He appears to be a good student.
The school bag is designed for users of his age.
His review was short enough to fit into the poster.
What he said supports the claims made in the poster.

explanation: A poster quotes a happy user to make its claims more believable. This is called a testimonial.

Match his words to the poster: 'Everything I need for school fits comfortably into it' supports 'Fit your entire school day into one bag'. 'I can also find and take out any item I need easily' supports 'a specific space for everything'.
Option (2) is tempting because he is 12, but the poster says the bag is 'Suitable for students of all ages', not only his age.
The answer is option (4).

questions.stem:
Based on Text 1, which of the following statements are true about the Peaks school bag?
A: The bag is small and light.
B: The bag comes in different colours.
C: The bag has multiple compartments.

explanation: A: The poster never says the bag is small or light. It says you can 'Fit your entire school day into one bag', which suggests a roomy bag. A is not supported.
B: 'Wide range of colours to choose from!' So B is true.
C: 'Get organised with a specific space for everything!' A separate space for each item means the bag has many compartments. So C is true.
B and C are true. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: What is the **main** message of Text 2?
options: Students should prioritise comfort when choosing a bag.
Students should choose school bags with more features.
Students should express their personality and personal style.
Students should use lockers or desks to store their belongings.

explanation: The main message is the idea that runs through the whole article, not one detail. Text 2 moves from 'bags look good' to 'have you considered the impact on your health?' and keeps returning to your back: 'fits comfortably on your back', 'reduce the pressure on your back', 'protect your back'.
So the writer wants students to put comfort and health before style when choosing and packing a bag. That is option (1).

Option (4) is tempting, but lockers and desks are introduced with 'For example'. They are one example of how to keep the bag light, not the main message. Option (3) is what many students do, not what the writer advises.
The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Text 1 and Text 2 express differing views on whether __________.
options: students can store certain items in school
school bags should look appealing to students
school bags can fit everything needed for school
students should fit everything into their school bags

explanation: Find a point where the two texts say opposite things.
Text 1 encourages it: 'Fit your entire school day into one bag, all your books, stationery, lunch boxes and more!'
Text 2 advises against it: 'health experts recommend packing only the items needed for the day' and 'leaving out unnecessary items'.
Option (3) is the trap. It is about whether a bag **can** fit everything, and Text 2 does not say it cannot. The disagreement is about whether students **should**. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: Find the subject: 'an astonishing **amount** of plastic waste'. The words 'enough to fill 2,000 garbage trucks' only describe the amount.
The waste does not dump anything; it is dumped by people. That is the passive voice: be + past participle ('dumped').

'amount' is singular and 'Every day' shows something that happens regularly, so use the present singular 'is'. 'are' is tempting because 'trucks' is right before the blank, but trucks are not the subject.
The answer is (J) is.

review.note: The key's letter for Q26 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a J, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'turn up' is a phrasal verb that means to appear, often unexpectedly.
'Surprisingly' tells us the plastic appeared somewhere unexpected: on the backs of hermit crabs.
The answer is (P) up: 'plastic waste has now turned up on the backs of hermit crabs'.

review.note: The key's letter for Q27 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a P, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank joins 'soft, curly bodies' to more information about them: '___ leave them vulnerable to predators'.
Rule: use the relative pronoun 'which' to add information about a thing. ('who' is for people.)
The answer is (Q) which: 'soft, curly bodies which leave them vulnerable to predators'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The sentence has two halves: 'their tails are fragile' and 'they must constantly look for empty shells'.
The first half is the reason for the second, so we need a connector of reason that can start a sentence.
The answer is (B) because: 'Because their tails are fragile, they must constantly look for empty shells'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: Who is being protected? The crabs are protecting the crabs. The doer and the receiver are the same.
Rule: when the subject and the object are the same, use a reflexive pronoun. 'they' pairs with 'themselves'.
The answer is (M) themselves: 'to protect themselves from hungry birds and fishes'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the blank is 'been observed', so we need has/have to make the present perfect passive.
The subject is '10 out of 16 land species', which is plural (10 species), so use 'have', not 'has'.
The answer is (F) have: '10 out of 16 land species have been observed wearing plastic waste'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The list goes from an ordinary item (bottle caps) to a surprising one (broken lightbulbs).
'even' is used to add something surprising or extreme to what was said before.
The answer is (C) even: 'such as bottle caps, and even broken lightbulbs'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'result in' is a fixed pair: to result in something means to cause it.
Fewer sea snails cause fewer natural shells. ('result from' would give the cause, which is the wrong way round here.)
The answer is (H) in: 'resulting in fewer natural shells for the crabs'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: To 'choose A over B' means to pick A instead of B.
The crabs pick plastic materials instead of traditional shells because plastic is lighter.
The answer is (L) over: 'crabs choose plastic materials over traditional shells'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'it is still unclear ___' is followed by something scientists are not sure about: are the crabs endangered or not?
Rule: use 'if' (or 'whether') to introduce a yes/no question inside a sentence.
The answer is (G) if: 'it is still unclear if hermit crabs are directly endangered by this behaviour'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++sequanse++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means the order in which things happen.
Spell it in two parts: se + quence. The ending is '-ence', as in 'sentence' and 'silence', and the 's' sound is spelt with a 'c'.
The correct word is 'sequence'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++accidental++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. The word describes how the object 'hit' the main character. A word that describes a verb is an adverb.
'accidental' is an adjective (an accidental hit). Add -ly to make the adverb: accidental + ly = accidentally. Keep both l's.
The correct word is 'accidentally'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++spreading++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. 'she quickly ___ her panic' needs a main verb in the simple past, like 'followed' and 'began' earlier in the paragraph. An -ing word cannot be the main verb without 'was'.
'spread' is an irregular verb: the past tense is also 'spread', not 'spreaded'.
The correct word is 'spread'.

review.note: The sentence is printed as 'spreading her panic all the other animals' (a 'to' seems to be missing after 'panic' where a correction was pasted over the line). It is transcribed as printed; the answer is not affected.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++thurruhly++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means completely or very much.
It is built from 'thorough' + ly. Remember the silent 'ough' at the end of 'thorough', as in 'borough'.
The correct word is 'thoroughly'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++seens++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The parts of a play are its 'scenes'.
'scene' has a silent 'c' after the 's'. Do not mix it up with 'seen', the past participle of 'see', which sounds the same.
The correct word is 'scenes'.

review.note: The key's word for Q40 is under the watermark; the visible letters read 'scenes', which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++dielog++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means the lines that the characters speak to each other.
It starts with 'dia-' (as in 'diagram') and, in British spelling, which Singapore schools use, it ends with '-logue' (as in 'catalogue').
The correct word is 'dialogue'. The answer key gives the shorter American spelling 'dialog', which is also accepted.

review.note: The key prints the American spelling 'dialog'. The British spelling 'dialogue' is the standard form taught in Singapore, so it is shown as the answer and 'dialog' is also accepted.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++jump++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look at the word in front: 'the importance **of** not ___'. 'of' is a preposition.
Rule: a verb that follows a preposition takes the -ing form. The word 'not' in between does not change this.
The correct word is 'jumping'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++valued++.

explanation: This is a word-form error. 'valued' means that someone treasures it (a valued friend). A lesson that is very useful and worth a lot is a 'valuable' lesson.
Form the adjective from 'value': drop the 'e' and add -able.
The correct word is 'valuable'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++rekkomend++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means to tell someone that something is good.
Think of it as re + commend: one 'c' and double 'm'. There is no 'k' in it.
The correct word is 'recommend'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++enjoying++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. 'anyone who ___ a fun story' needs a complete verb. An -ing word needs a helping verb ('is enjoying'), and there is none.
'anyone' is singular and the sentence states a general fact, so use the simple present singular: enjoys.
The correct word is 'enjoys'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: The boxes are sealed, so buyers find out what is inside only at the moment they open them.
'not ... until' means something does not happen before a certain point: 'do not know what they will get until they open them'.
'till' and 'before' give the same meaning.
The answer is 'until'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Although' signals a contrast: blind boxes **feel like** a modern trend, but in fact the idea is old.
The next sentence proves it: something similar was already common 'In the 1950's'. So 'the idea is not new'.
The answer is 'new'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'also known as' is a fixed phrase that introduces another name for something.
Mystery prize tickets had another name, Tikam-Tikam. Note that 'called' does not fit, because we say 'also called Tikam-Tikam' without 'as'.
The answer is 'known'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: The example after the blank is 'shoplifting', which is something people did. We need a plural noun for things people do.
The next sentence refers back to the same idea with 'such acts'. So the craze led people to extreme actions.
'acts', 'behaviour', 'measures' and 'lengths' also fit.
The answer is 'actions'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: The passage moves from the 1950's to the present: 'such acts **have also been** reported by shops selling blind boxes here'.
The present perfect tense ('have been reported') goes with a period of time leading up to now. 'In recent months' means in the last few months.
The answer is 'recent'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence is a question, and the next sentences answer it with 'One reason is ...' and 'Another reason is ...'.
A question that is answered with reasons begins with 'why'.
The answer is 'why'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: The next sentence talks about 'a rare piece'. Rare items are ones that there are not many of.
Something that there is not much of is 'limited in quantity'.
The answer is 'limited'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look at the words around the blank: 'a difficult ___ has been successfully completed'. We need a noun for something that can be difficult and can be completed.
Finding the rare piece feels like finishing a hard job: a difficult task. 'mission', 'quest' and 'challenge' also fit.
The answer is 'task'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: What do collectors share 'online through posts and live videos'? The next sentence tells us: others watch them 'unbox rare items'.
They are sharing what happened to them when they bought and opened the boxes: their experience.
'experiences', 'collections', 'purchases' and 'finds' also fit.
The answer is 'experience'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: Seeing others unbox rare items makes more people want to do the same thing.
The usual verb with 'trend' is 'follow': to follow a trend is to do what many others are doing. 'join the trend' is also used.
The answer is 'follow'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: The writer is comparing the excitement of blind boxes with gambling. In both, you pay without knowing what you will get.
The blank is followed by 'to', and 'similar to' means 'like'.
The answer is 'similar'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'in hopes of' (or 'in the hope of') is a phrase that means 'wishing to get'.
People keep buying because they wish for a rare item, 'only to end up with duplicates'.
'hope', 'search' and 'pursuit' also fit the pattern 'in ___ of getting'.
The answer is 'hopes'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: Clue: 'the behaviour may even become addictive'. Something addictive is very hard to give up.
So the cycle of buying again and again is 'hard to stop'. We also say 'break a cycle', so 'break' is just as good.
The answer is 'stop'.

review.note: First choice when solving was 'break' (to break a cycle); the key's 'stop' is equally right and is shown as the answer, with 'break' and other clear fits accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: The words after the blank explain it: 'where people frequently spend more than intended or buy repeatedly'.
A 'spending spree' is a short period when someone buys a lot without control. The blank needs the plural: sprees.
'spending habits' and 'spending patterns' also fit, because the passage says it happens 'frequently'.
The answer is 'sprees'.

review.note: First choice when solving was 'habits' (risky spending habits); the key's 'sprees' fits equally well and is shown as the answer. 'habits', 'patterns' and 'behaviour' are accepted as clearly correct in context.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank is joined to 'rules' by 'and', so we need a plural noun with a similar meaning.
The purpose is 'to better protect consumers', and the example is 'the ban on Tikam-Tikam'. A ban is a kind of restriction: a limit on what people may do.
'regulations' and 'laws' also fit.
The answer is 'restrictions'.

review.note: First choice when solving was 'regulations' (rules and regulations); the key's 'restrictions' is shown as the answer and 'regulations', 'laws' and similar words are accepted.

questions.stem:
"Did you paint this picture?" Mr Shelby asked his daughter.
Mr Shelby asked his daughter if ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Mr Shelby asked his daughter if she had painted that picture.

explanation: This changes a direct question into reported speech. After 'if', use statement word order (subject before verb), drop 'did' and end with a full stop, not a question mark.
Pronoun: 'you' is his daughter, so it becomes 'she'.
Tense: move one step back. The simple past 'did ... paint' becomes the past perfect 'had painted'.
Pointing word: 'this' becomes 'that'. Answer: Mr Shelby asked his daughter if she had painted that picture.

review.keyAnswer: Mr Shelby asked his daughter if she had painted that picture.
review.solvedAnswer: Mr Shelby asked his daughter if she had painted that picture.

questions.stem:
The prey never heard a sound because of the silent movement of the tiger.
So silently did ____________________ the prey never heard a sound.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: So silently did the tiger move that the prey never heard a sound.

explanation: The pattern is 'So + adverb + did + subject + base verb + that + result'. Starting with 'So silently' turns the word order around, like a question.
The noun phrase 'the silent movement of the tiger' must become a subject and a verb: the tiger moved silently. 'silent' has already become the adverb 'silently'.
After 'did', use the base form 'move', not 'moved', because 'did' already shows the past tense.
Join the result with 'that'. Answer: So silently did the tiger move that the prey never heard a sound.

review.keyAnswer: So silently did the tiger move that the prey never heard a sound.
review.solvedAnswer: So silently did the tiger move that the prey never heard a sound.

questions.stem:
Mike ignored the warning sign. He could have caused an accident.
By ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: By ignoring the warning sign, Mike could have caused an accident.

explanation: 'By' is a preposition that shows how something happened. A verb after a preposition takes the -ing form: 'ignored' becomes 'ignoring'.
Rule: the person doing the -ing action must be the subject of the main clause. So name 'Mike' right after the comma, in place of 'He'.
Keep 'could have caused an accident' exactly as it is, and put a comma after the 'By' phrase.
Answer: By ignoring the warning sign, Mike could have caused an accident.

review.keyAnswer: By ignoring the warning sign, Mike could have caused an accident.
review.solvedAnswer: By ignoring the warning sign, Mike could have caused an accident.

questions.stem:
Polly contributed generously to the local charity.
Polly made a ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Polly made a generous contribution to the local charity.

explanation: 'made a' must be followed by a noun, so the verb 'contributed' changes to the noun 'contribution'.
The adverb 'generously' described the verb. Now it has to describe a noun, so it changes to the adjective 'generous'.
The adjective goes before the noun: a generous contribution. Keep 'to the local charity'.
Answer: Polly made a generous contribution to the local charity.

review.keyAnswer: Polly made a generous contribution to the local charity.
review.solvedAnswer: Polly made a generous contribution to the local charity.

questions.stem:
Besides being long, the movie was also boring.
Not only was ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Not only was the movie long, but it was also boring.
accept: Not only was the movie long, it was also boring.

explanation: 'Besides being long ... also boring' means the movie was both long and boring. 'Not only ... but also' says the same thing.
When 'Not only' starts the sentence, the verb comes before the subject: 'Not only **was the movie** long'.
The second half goes back to normal word order and needs its own subject: 'but it was also boring'.
Answer: Not only was the movie long, but it was also boring.

review.keyAnswer: Not only was the movie long, but it was also boring.
review.solvedAnswer: Not only was the movie long, but it was also boring.

questions.stem: Why did Ryan "lay sleepless in the dark" (line 3, paragraph 1)?

answer.value: Ryan lay sleepless because it was his first time staying away from home and the thin, hard mattress made him miss his own comfortable bed.

explanation: Read on from 'Ryan lay sleepless in the dark'. The very next sentence gives the reason: 'This was his first time staying away from home, and the thin, hard mattress made him miss his own comfortable bed.'
The marker looks for two ideas for the 1 mark: he was away from home (for the first time), and his discomfort (he missed his own bed because the mattress was thin and hard).
Do not write only that the quiet forest made his heart beat faster. That describes how he felt, but the passage gives being away from home as the reason.

review.keyAnswer: It was his first time staying away from home and he missed his own bed. (Key points: 'Away from home' + discomfort)
review.solvedAnswer: First time staying away from home; the thin, hard mattress made him miss his own bed. Agrees with key.
review.note: The instruction on the question page reads 'answer questions 66 to 76' and the passage page has its printed numbers '71 to 80' struck out by hand; the comprehension questions are in fact 66 to 75, and the group instruction says so.

questions.stem:
Based on lines 5-10 (paragraph 2), which two pieces of information about Marcus tell us that he was a suitable group leader?
(Write two points, I and II.)

answer.value:
I) He was the only one who had mastered all the safety knots during the practice sessions in school.
II) He checked every classmate's harness with a sharp gaze.

explanation: Paragraph 2 says Marcus's appointment 'was no surprise', and the dash introduces the first reason: 'he was the only one who had mastered all the safety knots'. Keep the word 'only'; it shows he was the most skilled. (1 mark)
The second piece of information is what he did as leader: 'he checked every classmate's harness with a sharp gaze'. This shows he was responsible and careful about everyone's safety. (1 mark)
Each point must be a fact about Marcus from lines 5-10. 'He climbed the wall with ease' is from paragraph 3, so it does not count.

review.keyAnswer: He was the only one who had mastered all the safety knots during practice. [1m] OR Only Marcus had mastered all the safety knots. He checked every classmate's harness with a sharp gaze. [1m]
review.solvedAnswer: Only one who had mastered all the safety knots; checked every classmate's harness with a sharp gaze. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Explain clearly what caused Ryan to feel 'embarrassed' (line 14, paragraph 3).

answer.value: Ryan froze at the rock wall and Marcus shouted at him from above to start climbing, and the other students were watching him tremble.

explanation: 'Explain clearly' for 2 marks means two causes are needed. Both are in paragraph 3, around the word 'embarrassed'.
Cause 1, what happened at the wall: Ryan 'took one look at the sheer height of the wall and froze', and Marcus shouted at him from above, 'Don't just stand there! Start climbing!' (1 mark)
Cause 2, who saw it: 'the other students watched him tremble'. Being watched by his classmates while he shook with fear is what made it embarrassing. (1 mark)
Writing only 'Marcus shouted at him' gets 1 mark. Add that his classmates were watching him tremble.

review.keyAnswer: Reason 1 (1m) [Event at Wall]: Ryan froze at the wall / was unable to move at the wall / Marcus was shouting at him from above. Reason 2 (1m) [Being watched by peers]: His classmates were watching him tremble / shiver / shake.
review.solvedAnswer: He froze and Marcus shouted at him from above; the other students watched him tremble. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Based on information from lines 17-21 (paragraph 4, from "minded will to be the first group" to "kept his distance"), fill in the following table.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Marcus: What do his actions tell us about how he felt?

answer.value: Marcus felt angry (or: annoyed / irritated / impatient / agitated).

explanation: Marcus's actions in these lines: he 'snatched' Ryan's water bottle, 'shouted', 'shoved' the bottle into his own bag and 'stomped off'.
'snatched', 'shoved' and 'stomped' are all rough, forceful actions. They show he was angry, and impatient with Ryan for slowing the group down.
The marker accepts: angry, agitated, impatient, irritated or annoyed. Give a feeling word, not a description of what he did.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Ryan: What does his facial expression tell us about how he felt?

answer.value: Ryan felt shocked (or: surprised / caught off-guard).

explanation: The question asks about Ryan's **facial expression**. Find the look on his face: 'Ryan stared wide-eyed at Marcus's back.'
Eyes open wide show shock or surprise. He did not expect Marcus to snatch his bottle.

The marker accepts: surprised, shocked or caught off-guard. It must be an unpleasant kind of surprise, so do not write 'amazed' or 'excited'. 'Sad' (from 'felt his eyes moisten') is not what the key takes, because the wide-eyed stare is the facial expression.

review.keyAnswer: Marcus: angry / agitated / impatient / irritated / annoyed [1m]. Ryan: surprised / shocked / caught off-guard [1m] [Negative surprise] From 'stared wide-eyed'.
review.solvedAnswer: Marcus: angry / impatient. Ryan: shocked (stared wide-eyed). Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Based on lines 15-23 (paragraphs 4 and 5), state whether each statement in the table below is true or false, then give one reason why you think so.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Marcus has a competitive nature.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Marcus had a single-minded will to be the first group to reach the checkpoint.

explanation: A competitive person badly wants to win or be first. Look for that in paragraph 4.
'Marcus had a single-minded will to be the first group to reach the checkpoint.' 'Single-minded' means thinking about one aim only, and his aim was to be first.
So the statement is True. The reason must be this evidence, not the statement repeated.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Ryan could not control his emotions well.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: False. Ryan felt his eyes moisten (well up with tears), but he forced himself to keep walking in silence.

explanation: Find the moment Ryan's feelings were tested: after Marcus's outburst, 'Ryan felt his eyes moisten, but he forced himself to keep walking in silence.'
He was close to tears, but the word 'but' shows he held them back and carried on quietly. That is good control of his emotions.
So the statement is False. Give both halves: his eyes welled up, yet he forced himself to keep walking in silence.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
Ryan was still upset with Marcus during dinner.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. Ryan was in a sullen mood and sat alone at the edge of the campsite during dinner. (Or: He was still muttering that all Marcus cared about was that silly trophy.)

explanation: Paragraph 5 describes dinner: 'By evening, Ryan was in a sullen mood. During dinner, he sat alone at the edge of the campsite.' 'Sullen' means silent and bad-tempered.
He also muttered, 'All Marcus cares about is that silly trophy', which shows that his unhappiness was about Marcus.
So the statement is True. Either piece of evidence earns the mark.

review.keyAnswer: a) True --- Marcus had a single-minded will to be the first group to reach the checkpoint. b) False --- Ryan felt his eyes well up with tears, but he forced himself to keep walking in silence. c) True --- Ryan was sullen and sat alone at the edge of the campsite during dinner. Or He was still muttering that Marcus only cared about winning the trophy during dinner.
review.solvedAnswer: a) True; b) False; c) True, with the same evidence. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the words in the left column refer to in the passage?

parts.label: a

accept: the brass compass that belonged to Marcus's brother
the brass compass Marcus was holding

explanation: 'Marcus jumped and tried to hide **it**.' Ask: what was Marcus holding that he would want to hide?
Look back to paragraph 6: 'Marcus was holding the brass compass so tightly that his knuckles were white.' Later, in paragraph 7, he 'held up the compass'.
So 'it' refers to the (brass) compass. Extra detail, such as that it belonged to his brother, is fine.

parts.label: b

answer.value: Winning 'Best Camper' like his brother did (being just like his brother, as his parents expected).

explanation: Read the sentence before the phrase: 'He had won 'Best Camper' three years ago. My parents expect me to be just like him, but it's a Herculean task.'
A Herculean task is one that needs enormous effort. Here the task is what his parents expect: to be just like his brother, that is, to win 'Best Camper' too.
The marker looks for: (Marcus) winning 'Best Camper'. Writing only 'a very difficult task' explains the meaning of the phrase but does not say what it refers to.

review.keyAnswer: (a) the (brass) compass [1m] [accept relevant additional information, e.g. that belonged to Marcus' brother]. (b) (Marcus) winning 'Best Camper' [1m].
review.solvedAnswer: (a) the brass compass; (b) being just like his brother, i.e. winning 'Best Camper'. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Based on information from lines 24-31 (paragraph 6), fill in the following table.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Cause: Ryan saw Marcus sobbing and shaking.
Effect: __________

answer.value: Ryan's anger towards Marcus began to soften. (Ryan became less angry.)

explanation: Find the sentence that matches the cause: 'However, as he watched Marcus shaking, his anger began to soften.'
The word 'as' links the two: watching Marcus sob and shake is the cause, and Ryan's anger softening is the effect.
The marker accepts: Ryan's anger (towards Marcus) began to soften / Ryan became less angry / Ryan's anger faded.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Cause: __________
Effect: Marcus' knuckles turned white.

answer.value: Marcus held the (brass) compass very tightly.
accept: Marcus was holding the brass compass tightly.
Marcus was holding the compass tightly.
Marcus held the brass compass tightly.
Marcus was holding the brass compass so tightly.

explanation: Find the knuckles in paragraph 6: 'Marcus was holding the brass compass **so** tightly **that** his knuckles were white.'
'so ... that' is a cause-and-effect pattern. What comes after 'so' is the cause; what comes after 'that' is the effect.
Cause: Marcus was holding the compass tightly. Include the word 'tightly'; just 'holding the compass' is not enough.

review.keyAnswer: a) Ryan's anger towards Marcus began to soften. [1m] / Ryan became less angry. / Ryan's anger faded. b) Marcus held a/the compass tightly. [1m]
review.solvedAnswer: a) Ryan's anger began to soften; b) Marcus was holding the brass compass so tightly. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Marcus' reactions towards Ryan shifted greatly after the conversation from lines 32-37 (paragraph 7). What did Marcus do differently whenever Ryan struggled to complete an activity?

parts.label: a

answer.value: Marcus shouted (snapped / yelled) at Ryan and embarrassed him in front of the others.

explanation: Look at the two times Ryan struggled before the conversation. At the rock wall (paragraph 3): Marcus 'shouted from above', 'Don't just stand there! Start climbing!' On the hike (paragraph 4): he snatched the bottle and shouted, 'You're drinking too much and stopping too often!'
Both times he scolded Ryan loudly in front of the class instead of helping.
The marker accepts: snapped / yelled at him, humiliated him, embarrassed him, reprimanded him, or felt annoyed with him.

parts.label: b

answer.value: Marcus went over to help Ryan: he taught (guided / advised) him how to do it.

explanation: After the conversation, Ryan struggled again, this time to light his fire (paragraph 8).
This time 'Marcus came over and crouched beside him', showed him how to stack the fuel tablets and blocked the wind for him.
The marker accepts: taught him, guided him, advised him (helped him).

review.keyAnswer: Before the conversation: snapped / yelled at him, humiliated him, felt annoyed with him, embarrassed him, reprimanded him. After the conversation: taught him, guided him, advised him [rest of the line is under the watermark].
review.solvedAnswer: Before: shouted at / scolded him. After: came over and helped (taught) him. Agrees with key.
review.note: The end of the key's 'After the conversation' line is under the watermark; 'taught him, guided him, advised him' is readable. The paper prints no mark split; 1 mark is given to each box.

questions.stem:
Complete the diagram.
**How Marcus helped Ryan start a fire**
Box 1: __________
Box 2: __________
(Write the two ways, one for each box.)

answer.value:
Box 1: He showed (told) Ryan how to stack the fuel tablets, arranging them so that the flame would keep going.
Box 2: He used his own body to block the wind while Ryan tried again.

explanation: Everything Marcus did to help is in paragraph 8, after 'Marcus came over and crouched beside him'.
First way: '"Stack the fuel tablets like this. It keeps the flame going," he said, arranging them.' He told Ryan to stack the fuel tablets and arranged them to show how.
Second way: 'He used his own body to block the wind while Ryan tried again.' The breeze was what kept blowing the flame out.

The answer key lists 'arranged the fuel tablets' and 'told him to stack the fuel tablets' as the two answers. Blocking the wind is just as clearly stated in the passage (and the key itself uses it as evidence in question 75).

review.keyAnswer: - arranged the fuel tablets  - told him to stack the fuel tablets [the ends of both lines are under the watermark]

questions.stem:
"He nodded approvingly, thinking that sometimes, the most important lessons at camp had nothing to do with knots or rock walls." (lines 44-45, paragraph 9)
What did Mr Lim think Marcus and Ryan learnt from their time at camp? Support your answer with evidence from the passage.

answer.value: Mr Lim thought they had learnt to be kind and supportive towards each other (to empathise with others / the importance of friendship). Marcus came over to help Ryan when he was struggling to light his fire, and even used his own body to block the wind.

explanation: 'Knots or rock walls' stand for camp skills. Mr Lim meant the boys had learnt something about how to treat people instead. (Lesson, 1 mark)

The marker accepts lessons such as: to empathise with others, to be supportive, teamwork, patience, caring, kindness, understanding, resolving conflict, being grateful, or the importance of friendship.

Evidence (1 mark): it must be something Mr Lim saw. He 'watched the interaction between the two boys' in paragraph 8: Marcus came over to help Ryan when he was struggling to light the fire, and blocked the wind with his body.

The key says the evidence must come from lines 38-43 or from an earlier incident Mr Lim witnessed (the High Elements course or the hiking expedition). The night-time talk by the benches does not count, because Mr Lim was not there.

review.keyAnswer: Lesson: Mr Lim thought they learnt to empathise with others / to be supportive / about teamwork / patient / caring / kindness / understanding / resolve conflict / grateful / importance of friendship. [1m] Evidence: Marcus came over to help Ryan when he was struggling to light the fire (without being asked) / outdoor cooking session [1m]; Blocked the wind ... (start a fire) [1m]. Evidence must be from lines 38-43 or any earlier incidents that Mr Lim had witnessed e.g. High Elements course / hiking expedition.
review.solvedAnswer: They learnt kindness / empathy and to support each other; evidence: Marcus helped Ryan light the fire. Agrees with key.
